questions.q: What is the maximum number of records a single trigger invocation processes in one batch?
options: Unlimited — all records in a DML statement always fire the trigger together
questions.explain: Salesforce processes DML in batches of up to 200 records per trigger invocation; a 450-record insert fires the trigger three times (200, 200, 50).

questions.q: Why does a SOQL query placed inside a for loop over Trigger.new work fine in manual UI testing but fail during a bulk data load?
options: SOQL queries are disabled during manual testing
Manual testing typically exercises one record, so the query only runs once; a bulk load can run the same trigger with 200 records, running the query 200 times and exceeding governor limits
Bulk data loads use a different version of Apex
The query syntax itself is different in bulk operations
questions.explain: With one record, one query inside the loop is harmless; with 200 records in the batch, that same loop runs the query 200 times in one transaction, which can exceed the governor limit on SOQL queries.

questions.q: What is the correct bulk-safe pattern for querying related Account records from inside an Opportunity trigger?
options: Query once per Opportunity inside the loop, since each needs its own Account
Skip querying and rely only on Trigger.oldMap
Collect AccountIds into a Set, run one SOQL query with WHERE Id IN :accountIds, and store the results in a Map for lookup
Query all Accounts in the org with no WHERE clause, then filter in Apex
questions.explain: Collecting ids into a Set, querying once with IN, and building a Map keeps the number of SOQL queries constant regardless of batch size.

questions.q: Why is a Set<Id> used to collect AccountIds before querying, rather than a List<Id>?
options: A Set automatically removes duplicate Ids, so the same Account isn't queried or counted more than once unnecessarily
Set is the only collection type SOQL's IN clause accepts
A List cannot be used in a WHERE Id IN clause
Sets execute SOQL queries faster than Lists at runtime
questions.explain: Many Opportunities can share the same AccountId; a Set naturally deduplicates them, keeping the bulk query efficient regardless of how many Opportunities point to the same Account.

questions.q: Why should a bulkification test insert 200+ records rather than just one?
options: Apex requires exactly 200 records in every test method
A single-record test can pass even when SOQL/DML sits inside a loop, since the loop only runs once — the bug only appears once the batch is large enough to run it repeatedly
200 is the minimum number of records Salesforce allows in a test class
Smaller batches run slower than large ones, so large batches are used to test performance only
questions.explain: A bulkification bug is invisible with one record because the loop body only executes once either way; only a large batch exposes that SOQL/DML is running once per record instead of once per transaction.
